newsitem.title: JAPAN: Dlr/yen seen stuck in range, eyes on dlr/mark.
newsitem.headline: Dlr/yen seen stuck in range, eyes on dlr/mark.

text.p: The dollar is likely to remain stuck in a narrow range versus the Japanese currency in Asia on Tuesday, as the absence of fresh incentives for the dollar/yen is expected to keep market players focused on the dollar/mark and mark/yen, traders said.

"The dollar will probably hover between 113.50 yen and 114 yen in Asia. Japanese exporter offers are placed above 114 yen, but the dollar looks well-supported below 113.50 yen," said a trust bank trader.
Traders said they expect the dollar to test 1.8 marks again later today when European markets open.
In Monday's New York trade, the dollar twice charged towards 1.80 marks, but stopped just shy of the key level.

"Profit-taking could cap dollar/mark during Asian trading hours. Market players are also cautious that German officials might repeat comments expressing worries about the mark's weakness," said a city bank trader.
An overnight wire story was said to have quoted an anonymous Bundesbank official as saying the bank was concerned with the dollar above 1.75 marks, but not enough to intervene to support the mark.
Meanwhile, traders in Europe said on Monday that the Bank of Italy had bought mark/lira at 970, boosting the mark from a six-month low.
There were also rumours overnight that other authorities had also intervened to bolster the mark, including Scandinavian central banks.
The dollar's rise past 1.80 marks could pave the way for the German currency's fall below 63 yen, the trust bank trader said.
However, if position-squaring in mark/yen occurs, that might help push the dollar up to 114 yen, he added.
A lack of fresh incentives for the dollar/yen is expected to keep Tokyo players on hold ahead of a news briefing by senior finance ministry official Eisuke Sakakibara at 6.30 p.m. (0930 GMT).
Sakakibara, who currently heads MOF's International Finance Bureau, is to hold a news conference after his official appointment as the new vice finance minister for international affairs.
The outgoing MOF vice minister for international affairs, Takatoshi Kato, will also attend the news briefing.
